note.question: How should a government design crop-backed loans so that cash-constrained farmers do not strategically oversell at harvest, while improving both aggregate revenue and its distribution?
note.overview: Farmers simultaneously choose how much crop to sell after harvest, internalizing the price effects of one another’s sales. The government moves first when it designs a warehouse-receipt loan, and farmer behavior is solved in Nash equilibrium under that policy.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The government first announces a homogeneous or targeted warehouse-receipt loan. Farmers then simultaneously choose harvest-period sales, store the remainder, receive any collateralized loan, and sell stored crops in the lean period before repayment. Selling more at harvest satisfies cash needs but depresses the common first-period price. High-output farmers may strategically store more when low-output farmers oversell.

The government optimizes policy anticipating those responses.
